title: Quarterly Leadership Braintrust & Risk Roundup
summary: Leadership convened to review enterprise risk posture, hiring cadence, near-term product priorities to hit Q3 cost and latency targets, and to align on a contingency plan for capacity shortfalls. Decisions: prioritize Private deployment security workstream and defer two low-priority integrations; action items and owners assigned for benchmarks, hiring plan, and incident runbook updates.
action_items: Marcus Liu: Run 95th-percentile latency runbook test and share spreadsheet by 2026-05-07
Sofia Martínez: Prepare Private deployment SOC2 pre-check checklist by 2026-05-05
Noah Patel: Finalize Q3 hiring cadence and offer timeline for infra SREs by 2026-05-10
Priya Ramesh: Re-scope two integrations and publish updated roadmap by 2026-05-12
Elena Park: Send list of top 12 enterprise renewal dates + risk indicators to RevOps by 2026-05-04
next_steps: Share risk-deck and cost-sensitivity model (link in notes)
Schedule follow-up deep-dive with SE team on KV cache regressions, week of 2026-05-11
Ops to run a simulated region failover on 2026-05-18 and report results
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-30
Start: 10:00 PT
Duration: 1h15m (approx)
Attendees: Avery Chen, Jordan Kim, Marcus Liu, Priya Ramesh, Sofia Martínez, Noah Patel, Elena Park
Recorded by: Fireflies.ai

[00:00] Avery Chen: Okay, good morning everyone, um uh let's get started. Thanks for making time for the leadership braintrust. We've got a packed agenda — risk, hiring, product triage. Jordan, you want to do a quick top-line?
[00:23] Jordan Kim: Yeah thanks Avery. Quick context — Q2 is shaping up fine but we have a tight runway for meeting our committed latency SLOs for a handful of large customers. There's also some pressure on Dedicated reservations from a couple renewals. So today is: identify operational risks, agree prioritization, and lock owners.
[00:45] Marcus Liu: Quick one, I want to flag the KV cache regression we saw in the Santa Clara cluster — um so the 95th pct latency jumped when we changed the batching heuristic. I know the SEs are on it but we need a leadership decision on whether to roll that heuristic back for dedicated pools.
[01:10] Priya Ramesh: Can you give a short quant? I remember seeing a spike to 320ms 95th when baseline was like 180, something like that?
[01:18] Marcus Liu: Yeah, roughly. There's some noise in the telemetry, and also the metric labeling got munged in the pipeline so our dashboards underreport. We're cleaning that up.
[01:30] Sofia Martínez: And to add, our autoscaler behaved differently than expected under burst traffic because the batching threshold held requests longer, so latency hurt. There's a tuning knob we can flip, but it trades cost for lower p95.
[01:48] Elena Park: From the sales side, a few renewal conversations escalated. One enterprise asked for a private deployment timeline and SOC2 evidence before committing. So we need to align product + infra on what we can promise.
[02:05] Noah Patel: And on hiring — we have offers out to three infra SREs, two candidates asked for slightly higher comp bands. If we delay offers we risk losing pipeline capacity.
[02:18] Avery Chen: Right, so items: one is an immediate incident-runbook update for the KV cache/batching issue; two is a prioritization decision on private deployment security artifacts; three is hiring timeline. Let's walk through each. Marcus, runbook first.
[02:36] Marcus Liu: Sure. We have an imperfect runbook: step 1 isn't explicit about rolling rollback of batching heuristics. During the incident it took the on-call team too long to decide. I propose a clear fail-safe: if p95 crosses 250ms for 10 minutes, auto-scale down batching and enable low-latency mode for dedicated pools.
[02:58] Jordan Kim: That sounds reasonable. We should also ensure the fallback is reversible and covered by a short postmortem.
[03:08] Priya Ramesh: Also, for Product, low-latency mode has UI and cost implications. We can't toggle it blindly for hosted customers without informing them about cost delta. We need an opt-in for hosted and a forced toggle for our Dedicated / Reserved customers under SLA.
[03:28] Sofia Martínez: Agreed. Technically we can enforce by routing policy — tag dedicated pools. But we need the dashboard + alerting to reflect that.
[03:38] Avery Chen: Action: Marcus to run the test and produce the artifact. Marcus, due date?
[03:44] Marcus Liu: I'll run the 95th-percentile tests and share a spreadsheet by 2026-05-07.
[03:49] Avery Chen: Good. Next, SOC2/private deployment asks. Priya?
[03:54] Priya Ramesh: Security and compliance is the gating factor for a number of deals. We have a partial SOC2 pack but not the pre-check checklist that enterprises ask for. Sofia, can infra collate the pre-check items we can give to prospects?
[04:08] Sofia Martínez: Yes, we'll compile a Private deployment SOC2 pre-check checklist. It'll include KMS integrations, network isolation diagrams, audit log retention guarantees, and our incident cadence. We'll get a first draft by 2026-05-05.
[04:22] Elena Park: If we can provide that within 2 weeks it materially helps conversion. A couple of customers are on conditional holds.
[04:30] Jordan Kim: On that note, competition — CloudAI Inc is pitching a compliance-first angle, some prospects think CloudAI has better enterprise creds. We need crisp materials.
[04:41] Avery Chen: Okay add that to the deck. Speaking of the deck, Priya you'll own the risk-deck update?
[04:49] Priya Ramesh: Yes, I'll update the risk-deck and push to the leadership drive, include cost-sensitivity models and the two-scenario plan: conservative (flip batching knob) and aggressive (re-architect Batcher).
[05:02] Noah Patel: Hiring piece: our offer acceptance pattern suggests we need to move faster on comp approvals. If we want three infra hires in Q2, comp approvals should be expedited by hiring committee. I recommend we pre-approve a comp range for SREs to speed offers.
[05:17] Jordan Kim: Fine, we can approve a temporary higher band for the next month. Avery will sign off on the comp band?
[05:24] Avery Chen: I can approve up to the band we discussed offline; Noah send me a firm list and I'll sign them by 2026-05-03.
[05:31] Noah Patel: Great. I'll send the list today.
[05:35] [crosstalk] Marcus Liu: Quick question on product triage — Priya, which two integrations are we deferring?
[05:42] Priya Ramesh: The analytics connector v2 and the low-priority ephemeral tokens feature. Both are lower revenue impact and would free up two engineer-weeks for infra tuning.
[05:52] Marcus Liu: Fine with that. We need those engineer-weeks on the KV cache and batching rewrite.
[05:58] Priya Ramesh: Noted.
[06:01] Elena Park: On renewals: I collated the top 12 renewals; three are high-risk due to unmet compliance requests. I'll share the spreadsheet and flag the ones needing SOC2 evidence.
[06:12] Avery Chen: Perfect. Put that in Ops channel.
[06:15] Jordan Kim: Also want to talk about contingency routing and fallback policies. If our primary region saturates, do we have an automated fallback to cheaper model variants or the hosted fallback? Sofia?
[06:28] Sofia Martínez: We have a fallback but it's coarse right now. We can route to smaller-parameter model variants, but some customers expect parity. We should make fallbacks explicit in SLAs and have a separate 'degradation plan' per customer tier.
[06:43] Priya Ramesh: Let's prepare two demo scripts: one for canary rollback to smaller models, one for region failover. SEs need those to set expectations.
[06:52] Marcus Liu: SEs — can you run a simulated runbook with the SE + infra team next week? I'd like to see latency impact numbers.
[06:59] Elena Park: Yes, we can do that.
[07:02] Avery Chen: Good. Next, cost-sensitivity: we ran early numbers on quantization + batching trade-offs. The model quant recommendations could save up to 18% per-token cost but might increase error-rates slightly. Priya, do we have a plan for quality regression monitoring?
[07:20] Priya Ramesh: Yep, Optimize + evals team will put together a small regression suite tied to a key prompt-set per customer segment. We'll flag regressions automatically. Deliverable by 2026-05-12.
[07:31] Jordan Kim: And on finance, we need a short-term forecast for dedicated capacity vs hosted margin. Avery?
[07:38] Avery Chen: I'll produce a sensitivity table in the deck. Expect it in 48 hours.
[07:43] Marcus Liu: One more operational note: telemetry naming is inconsistent — sometimes KV cache appears as KV_cache, sometimes as kvcache, and the alert rule references the wrong series. This caused delayed detection. Ops needs standardization.
[07:56] Sofia Martínez: We'll run a telemetry normalization sweep and check alert bindings. I'll own that and report back.
[08:03] Priya Ramesh: Also, let's ensure the UX on the console makes the low-latency toggle explicit for dedicated customers so sales can show it in demos.
[08:11] Elena Park: Yes, please. That would help close deals faster.
[08:15] Avery Chen: We're getting near time. Quick recap: Marcus runs the p95 tests and updates runbook (due 2026-05-07); Sofia produces SOC2 pre-check for Private (due 2026-05-05) and telemetry sweep; Noah finalizes hiring offers (due 2026-05-03); Priya updates risk deck and roadmap scoping (due 2026-05-12); Elena shares renewal spreadsheet (due 2026-05-04); Ops to schedule simulated failover week of 2026-05-18.
[08:45] Jordan Kim: Anything else?
[08:47] Marcus Liu: Quick clarifying — do we commit to rolling back the batching heuristic immediately on customer-impacting incidents, or do we wait for the test results?
[08:58] Avery Chen: If an incident meets the defined threshold in the runbook (p95>250ms for 10m), do the safe rollback immediately. We will run the tests in parallel but rollback is allowed by the runbook.
[09:13] Noah Patel: I'll also prep a comms plan for internal ops and for customers affected by rollback.
[09:20] Priya Ramesh: I'll draft the customer communication templates — short note + FAQ — and share.
[09:27] Avery Chen: Great. Thanks everyone. I'll circulate the notes and the links: risk-deck, cost model, and renewal spreadsheet. Meeting adjourned.
[09:35] [end recording]

Notes and links referenced in meeting: "Risk & Ops Deck (internal)" link: https://redwood.company/drive/risk-deck-2026-04 (internal), "Renewal spreadsheet" link: https://redwood.company/drive/renewals-q2 (internal).

Transcription artifacts: there are occasional mis-hearings (e.g., "K V cash" vs "KV cache"), and some speaker attribution may be approximate in overlapping sections.
